assertions: Output launches multiple goroutines (e.g. 16) calling GetOrLoad concurrently with the same key
Output asserts the underlying fetch function was called exactly once, not just that all callers received the same value
Output asserts all goroutines received the same non-error result
Output uses sync.WaitGroup (or equivalent) to wait for all goroutines before asserting
Output does not rely on a value-only check that would still pass if fetch were called multiple times returning the same value
Output runs CreateOrder concurrently from multiple goroutines with the same idempotencyKey
Output asserts exactly one row exists in the DB for that key after all goroutines complete, via a count query
Output does not assert only that no error occurred, without checking the resulting row count
Output includes a case verifying a failed/erroring create does not leave a partial row behind
Output injects a generate function that returns a colliding value on the first call and a valid one on a later call, to prove the retry path re-attempts
Output does not only test the happy path where the first generated value succeeds immediately
Output includes a case where every attempt collides, asserting the exhausted-attempts error is returned after maxAttempts tries
Output asserts the exact number of generate() calls made, not just the final outcome
Output maintains an explicit list of every env key Load() reads (PORT, TIMEOUT, LOG_LEVEL) and resets all of them via t.Setenv before the defaults test
Output asserts the loaded Config equals a full expected Config{} struct literal in one comparison, not field-by-field assertions
Output does not leave any of the three env keys unreset before checking defaults
Test would fail if a new field were added to Config but not to the env-key reset list (i.e. the assertion is a full-struct comparison, not partial)
Output includes a nil-error test case
Output includes a generic/unrelated error case (e.g. errors.New("boom")) asserting IsRetryable returns false
Output includes individual cases for both ErrNotFound (expected false) and ErrConflict (expected true), tested directly rather than only through a code path that happens to produce them
Output uses a table-driven structure (a slice of test cases with a name/input/expected fields) rather than separate ad hoc test functions
